text: Switching from npm install to bun install makes installs up to 25x faster in any Node.js project
quote: Switch from `npm install` to `bun install` in any Node.js project to make your installations up to 25x faster.

text: Publishes benchmark timings comparing bun install with npm (0.21s vs 4.45s)
Built-in Node.js-compatible package manager meant as a faster replacement for npm, yarn, and pnpm
quote: The `bun` CLI contains a Node.js-compatible package manager designed to be a dramatically faster replacement for `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm`.

text: Works as a standalone tool in existing Node.js projects that have a package.json
quote: It's a standalone tool that works in existing Node.js projects; if your project has a `package.json`, you can use `bun install`.

text: Automatically migrates yarn.lock v1, package-lock.json (v2-4), and pnpm-lock.yaml to bun.lock on first install
quote:
When you run `bun install` in a project without a `bun.lock`, Bun automatically migrates existing lockfiles:

*   `yarn.lock` (v1)
*   `package-lock.json` (npm, `lockfileVersion` 2, 3 or 4)
*   `pnpm-lock.yaml` (pnpm)

text: Can write a Yarn lockfile alongside bun.lock
quote: To write a Yarn lockfile _in addition_ to `bun.lock`: bun install --yarn

text: Uses a text-based bun.lock lockfile by default since v1.2
quote: Bun v1.2 changed the default lockfile format to the text-based `bun.lock`.

text: Frozen-lockfile mode installs the exact locked versions without updating the lockfile, for reproducible installs
quote: For reproducible installs, use `--frozen-lockfile`. Bun installs the exact versions specified in the lockfile and does not update it.

text: Can generate a lockfile without installing anything into node_modules
quote: To generate a lockfile without installing to `node_modules`, use the `--lockfile-only` flag.

text: Install handles dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, and peerDependencies by default
quote: Installs all `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, and `optionalDependencies`. Bun installs `peerDependencies` by default.

text: Production install mode skips devDependencies
quote: To install in production mode (without `devDependencies`):

text: Installs packages globally with -g/--global, for example to get command-line tools
quote: To install a package globally, use the `-g`/`--global` flag. Use it to install command-line tools.

text: Offline mode never touches the network and fails if a required dependency is not cached
quote: Never touch the network (registry, tarball URLs, git); a required dependency that is not cached is an error

text: Keeps a global package cache at ~/.bun/install/cache, with the location configurable through BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR
quote: Bun stores every package downloaded from the registry in a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`, or the path set by the `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` environment variable.

text: Uses hardlinks on Linux and Windows so each package's contents exist in only one place on disk
quote: On Linux and Windows, Bun uses hardlinks to "copy" a module into a project's `node_modules` directory, so the contents of the package only exist in a single location on disk.

text: Does not run dependency lifecycle scripts like postinstall by default, for security
quote: Unlike other npm clients, Bun does not execute arbitrary lifecycle scripts like `postinstall` for installed dependencies.

text: Allows lifecycle scripts only for packages listed in trustedDependencies
quote: To tell Bun to allow lifecycle scripts for a particular package, add the package to `trustedDependencies` in your package.json.

text: Sets the maximum number of concurrent lifecycle scripts with --concurrent-scripts
quote: To adjust the maximum number of concurrent scripts, use the `--concurrent-scripts` flag.

text: Audits bun.lock packages against the npm advisory endpoint without needing node_modules
quote: Bun reads the package list from `bun.lock` (no `node_modules` required), sends it to the npm advisory endpoint, and prints a report.

text: Audit fix upgrades each vulnerable package to the lowest non-vulnerable version all dependents allow, then installs
quote: Runs the audit, then upgrades each vulnerable package to the lowest non-vulnerable version that every dependent's range allows, and installs.

text: Filters audit output by minimum severity using --audit-level
quote: `--audit-level=<low|moderate|high|critical>` - Only report vulnerabilities at this severity or higher

text: Supports npm-style workspaces for developing several packages in one monorepo
quote: Bun supports [`workspaces`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v9/using-npm/workspaces?v=true#description) in `package.json`. With workspaces, you develop several independent packages in a single repository, a _monorepo_.

text: Accepts full glob syntax, including negative patterns, in the workspaces field
quote: Bun supports full glob syntax in `"workspaces"`, including negative patterns such as `!**/excluded/**`.

text: Monorepo packages can reference each other with semver ranges or the workspace: protocol
quote: To reference another package in the monorepo, use a semver range or the workspace protocol (for example `workspace:*`)

text: Installs dependencies for a subset of workspaces using --filter patterns, including exclusions
quote: Install dependencies for all workspaces starting with `pkg-` except for `pkg-c`

text: A workspace marked self-contained acts as a hoisting barrier, so its node_modules holds a complete tree
quote: Mark such a workspace as self-contained... For that workspace `bun install` then behaves as a hoisting barrier — nothing it depends on... is placed above `apps/desktop/node_modules`

text: Defines shared dependency versions once in a root catalog and references them with the catalog: protocol
quote: When many packages need the same dependency versions, define those versions once in a catalog in the root `package.json` and reference them from your workspaces with the `catalog:` protocol.

text: Supports npm overrides and Yarn resolutions to set versions of transitive dependencies
quote: Bun supports npm's `"overrides"` and Yarn's `"resolutions"` in `package.json`. Both specify a version range for _metadependencies_

text: Supports patching dependencies
quote: npm-compatible, up to 30× faster. Workspaces, catalogs, overrides, patches and a lockfile you can read.

text: bun add adds a package to package.json
quote:
To add a particular package:

bash terminal icon="terminal"
bun add preact

text: Adds packages as dev, optional, or peer dependencies using --dev, --optional, or --peer
quote: Bun writes the package to `dependencies` unless you pass `--dev`, `--optional`, or `--peer`.

text: --exact writes the exact resolved version into package.json instead of a range
quote: To pin a package to the resolved version, use `--exact`. Bun writes the exact version number to your `package.json` instead of a version range.

text: --catalog writes the version to the root catalog and adds a catalog: reference in the current package
quote: In a workspace, `--catalog` writes the version to the root `package.json` catalog and adds `"catalog:"` to the current package.

text: bun remove deletes a package from every dependency group in package.json and updates bun.lock
quote: Bun removes the package from every dependency group in `package.json` that lists it and updates `bun.lock`.

text: In a monorepo, can remove a package from matching workspaces instead of the current package
quote: In a monorepo, remove the package from the matching workspace(s) instead of the current directory's package

text: bun update moves all direct and transitive dependencies to the newest versions their ranges allow
quote: `bun update` (alias `bun up`) updates every dependency, direct and transitive, to the newest version allowed by the ranges that request it.

text: Interactive update mode lets you choose which packages to update
quote: Use the `--interactive` flag to choose which packages to update

text: Updates a nested transitive dependency without adding it to package.json
quote: `bun update caniuse-lite` picks up a nested fix without adding it to your `package.json`.

text: bun dedupe collapses duplicate versions onto the smallest set of locked versions and saves the lockfile
quote: `bun dedupe` collapses these onto the smallest set of already-locked versions (preferring newer ones), saves `bun.lock`, and installs.

text: bun prune removes anything in node_modules that the current lockfile would not install
quote: `bun prune` deletes everything in `node_modules` that the current `bun.lock` would not install

text: bun outdated shows a table of dependencies with newer versions available
quote: `bun outdated` displays a table of the dependencies in your project that have newer versions available.

text: bun why shows the dependency chain explaining why a package is installed
quote: `bun why` explains why a package is installed in your project by showing the dependency chain that led to it.

text: bun info prints npm registry metadata such as latest version, description, homepage, and dependencies
quote: `bun info react` prints the package's latest version, description, homepage, dependencies, and other metadata.

text: Lists installed dependencies and their resolved versions
quote: To print a list of installed dependencies in the current project and their resolved versions, excluding their dependencies:

text: Lists every installed package grouped by license
quote: List every installed package grouped by license, as read from each package's `package.json` in `node_modules`.

text: Shows a diff between two package versions, including files and lines changed and notable package.json changes
quote: Show what changed between two versions of a package: a summary of the files and lines touched, the `package.json` changes worth a second look

text: bun pm pack creates a .tgz of publishable files using npm pack rules
quote: `bun pm pack` creates a `.tgz` file containing all files that would be published to npm, following the same rules as `npm pack`.

text: bun publish packs the package and replaces catalog and workspace protocols with resolved versions
quote: `bun publish` packs your package into a tarball and strips catalog and workspace protocols from the `package.json`, resolving versions if necessary.

text: Recursive publish releases the root and all workspace packages, dependencies before their dependents
quote: `--recursive` (`-r`) publishes the root package and every workspace package, dependencies before their dependents.

text: bun link registers a local package and symlinks it into another project's node_modules
quote: This command creates a symlink in the target project's `node_modules` directory pointing to the local directory.

text: bunx runs a package's executable without installing it
quote: bunx cowsay 'Hello, world!'   # execute a package
